a single administration of an adenovirus vector encoding human Gaa (hGAA), the gene defective in GSD-II patients, resulted in long-term correction of glycogen accumulations and improved cardiac function in a mouse model of the disease.

the long-term efficacy of adenovirus-mediated gene transfer of human acid-glucosidases to a mouse model of glycogen storage disease II was demonstrated by the persistence of the enzyme in muscle for at least six months, and the correction of pathologic glycogen accumulation in the heart.

the development of a gene therapy for GSD-II using an adenoviral vector encoding the hGAA cDNA.

the development of novel gene therapy strategies for the treatment of glycogen storage disease (GSD) types II (Pompe disease) and III, two rare, fatal, lysosomal storage disorders (LSDs) that result from a lack of the lysosomal enzyme alpha-glucosidases (GAA).
the development of novel gene therapy strategies to correct the pathophysiology of GSD-II.

the data demonstrate that a single injection of the Ad vector encoding hGAA results in long-term persistence in liver tissues, long-term persistence in all muscle groups analyzed, and long-term correction of intramuscular glycogens accumulations in all muscles analyzed.

a single injection of an adenoviral vector encoding human acid-alpha-glusosidase (hGAA), into the liver of a mouse model of glycogen storage disease (GSD)-II, resulted in long-term correction of glycogen accumulations within cardiac and skeletal muscle groups.

this study demonstrates that a single injection of an Ad vector encoding the human GAA gene into a mouse model of glycogen storage disease II results in the long-term persistence of vector-encoded hGAA mRNA and protein, which in turn is associated with a long-term correction of intramuscular glycogens accumulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results demonstrate that a single vector injection of Ad-hGAA into a GSD-II mouse model resulted in long-term correction of the pathologic intracellular glycogen accumulation, as well as long-term correction of cardiac glycogen accumulation.
the long-term persistence of adenovirus-mediated GAA expression in the liver of GSD-II knockout mice resulted in long-term correction of cardiac glycogen storage disease.

we have shown that a single intravenous injection of Ad vector encoding hGAA can be taken up by the liver and can persistently secrete hGAA protein, which is then taken up by all skeletal and cardiac muscle groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the liver can be used as a "depot" for the production of secreted therapeutic proteins that can then be taken up by the target tissue and provide long-term correction of a metabolic defect.
gene therapy can be effective in the treatment of glycogen storage disease II (GSDII), which is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by a mutation in the GAA gene.
a single vector injection of a gene encoding an enzyme that is secreted from the liver into the bloodstream, can persist for a long period of time in the bloodstream and in all tissues of the body.
